page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-144-lssd is an x86_64 instance built on the Intel Xeon 6985P-C architecture, delivering 144 dedicated vCPUs across 72 physical cores clocked at 2.3 GHz. The hardware architecture incorporates a 504 MB L3 cache along with support for Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector instruction sets. The server is configured with 1116 GB of memory, equating to 7.75 GB per vCPU, and integrates 9648 GB of local NVMe SSD storage spanning 24 drives. No discrete graphics processors are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core execution capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 156171.55 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 20930.0. Memory throughput benchmarks register 533.92 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 205.9 GB/sec for large-block writes. The configuration also achieves top-tier results in Redis operations at 219.47 million operations per second and PassMark database operations at 35978.12. In contrast, single-core processing capabilities are balanced, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring within the middle 50% band.

The bundled NVMe storage and vast memory footprint offer favorable qualitative resource density for infrastructure consolidation. Rather than provisioning multiple smaller compute instances, this configuration allows memory-bound services to operate on a single host. The system is well matched for high-throughput relational databases, large-scale in-memory key-value stores like Redis, data caching tiers, and multi-threaded CPU inference tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-144-lssd is a memory-dense compute configuration equipped with 144 vCPUs across 72 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz. The x86_64 platform includes 1116 GB of RAM, a 504 MB L3 cache, and 9648 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity across 24 drives, without dedicated GPUs. Standardized benchmarks place this instance in the top tier for multi-core processing, static web serving throughput, PassMark database operations, and Redis operations reaching 219.47 million operations per second, alongside uncached memory read bandwidth of 533.92 GB/sec. While single-thread execution sits in the mid-tier, the aggregate core density and large memory footprint provide high throughput per host. The server is structured to support large-scale enterprise databases, distributed in-memory data tiers, batch processing pipelines, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
